rule.description: A god class is an owner declaration (a class, a module-level object literal used as a manager object, or a flat module of many top-level function-like declarations) whose declared members number at least 10 and whose member bodies structurally span at least 4 distinct, unrelated responsibility groups among: css-styling, responsive-media, platform-lifecycle, listener-lifecycle, keyboard-policy, state-coordination, dom-traversal. Owner shape is deliberately irrelevant (class arm, manager-object arm, flat-function-hub arm), so re-hosting the same concentration under a different syntactic shape is still detected.

checks.description: Detect an owner declaration that concentrates many members spanning several unrelated responsibility groups.
checks.detected_relation: coordinating owner -> responsibility groups absorbed from the component/hook modules that delegate into it
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A single owner accumulates styling, responsive-media, platform-resource, listener, keyboard, state-coordination and DOM-navigation responsibilities that the surrounding modules route through it instead of owning, so unrelated changes all land in one declaration and every consumer couples to that declaration (god class).

matches.evidence: 'ProSidebarManager' (class) is a god class: it declares 21 members spanning 7 unrelated responsibilities [css-styling, dom-traversal, keyboard-policy, listener-lifecycle, platform-lifecycle, responsive-media, state-coordination]. The class is the single hub the sidebar shell, the menu tree components and two hooks reach into: entry E1 is the hub declaration itself, and entries E2-E9 are the delegating sites whose responsibilities (breakpoint media-query policy and off-canvas layout CSS, shared menu/element style resolution and menu-button CSS, popper instance creation/observation/visibility policy, portal-host lookup, keyboard activation/dismiss/toggle policies, accordion and active-descendant state transitions, inert-content props, breakpoint match-listener lifecycle) now live in it.

excluded.reason: Data-only constant tables (class-name maps and string constants). The rule targets behavior-bearing members; lookup tables declare no responsibilities to concentrate.
Individual styled declarations for one element each; each holds a single presentation responsibility and stays far below any concentration threshold.
Not production code; the rule scans only src/**/*.ts and src/**/*.tsx.
